answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may submit bids, with the bond slashable for provable fraud and returned only after a long challenge window. This makes a sybil swarm costly: an attacker must tie up real capital for each identity, while splitting one stake across many names does not create more voting or bidding weight. The bond is no oasis or haven from risk; a reef of independent challengers can expose copied credentials and trigger the penalty.
